claim: Adaptive pulse duration based on target range feedback reduces sea clutter false alarms while maintaining detection performance
mechanism: The radar system continuously estimates target range and adjusts pulse duration accordingly. Shorter pulses are used for near targets to maintain resolution, while longer pulses are used for distant targets to increase energy on target and improve signal-to-clutter ratio.
evidence: Bioacoustic systems in bats demonstrate adaptive pulse emission based on target distance
LFM waveforms show range-dependent clutter characteristics
Existing radar systems use pulse duration adjustments for specific scenarios
assumptions: Range estimation accuracy is sufficient for pulse adaptation
Sea clutter characteristics vary predictably with range
Pulse duration changes do not introduce significant range-Doppler coupling
FPGA hardware can implement real-time pulse generation switching
expected_failure_modes: Range-Doppler coupling becomes problematic at certain pulse durations
Switching between pulse durations introduces range ambiguities
novelty_rationale: Unlike fixed waveform systems, this approach dynamically optimizes pulse parameters based on real-time environmental feedback, similar to how bioacoustic systems adapt their signals
testability: Can be implemented by modifying existing radar pulse generation algorithms to include range-dependent pulse duration control
falsifier: If the system shows increased false alarm rates or reduced detection probability when implementing adaptive pulse duration compared to fixed LFM waveforms across all target ranges
